notes:
Renault and Dacia cars of the CAN era, scoped to cars up to about the 2018 model year: 11-bit CAN at 500 kbit/s on the OBD-II socket, ISO 15765-2, core units only. The 2018 cut-off is an inference, not a sourced date: it is chosen to stay clear of the security gateway that reports say recent cars carry, and no source read gives the model or year from which it appears.

The ten units are the addresses CanZE lists for the Twingo III phase 2 (the sonar row comes from the CanZE Zoe file, which has no sonar in the Twingo's) and the ddt4all address table lists for the whole Alliance; ddt4all's table is the same in its Clio IV, Captur, Megane IV, Duster and Sandero projects, so one address plan serves them, but neither source says which of these units a given Clio, Captur, Megane, Duster or Sandero fits, and the engine and gearbox rows come from a small-car file and may not match a given engine control unit. Whether these units speak UDS or KWP2000 over CAN on these cars was not established: UDS comes from the CanZE files for the Zoe and Twingo, and ddt4all supports both. Treat every row as unconfirmed on a given car until `obd-read probe` shows the unit answering. The Mercedes-Benz Citan W415 is covered the same way: ddt4all's project list has a "Daimler Citan" project (code VS10, with VS11 for the later Citan II) whose address table is the same Alliance-wide one, so the Citan is a Renault Alliance car for addressing; no source says which of these units a Citan fits, and the 2018 cut-off applies to it as to the others.

Session: the default session, 0x01, which every UDS unit must accept; the Twingo file gives 0x03 for these units, which the guard also permits.

Security gateway: a Renault security gateway is reported on recent cars, so a silent unit may be filtered rather than absent, and the tool reports a silent unit as no response, not as absent. A ddt4all issue (cedricp/ddt4all issue 404, Clio V, 2020) reports reads working through the OBD socket with writes blocked by a central gateway, and vendor pages (a Delphi article on a Renault Arkana, a Hella Gutmann page) say that fault codes and parameters can be read without unlocking it; none of them says which units a locked gateway hides from a read.
name: renault-dacia-core
description: Renault and Dacia CAN-era core units (Clio IV and V, Captur, Megane IV, Duster, Sandero) and the Mercedes-Benz Citan W415, UDS over 11-bit CAN, address plan from CanZE and ddt4all

vin.source: The WMIs are the makers' car and SUV identifiers in the world manufacturer identifier table of the Wikipedia article Vehicle identification number, which cites the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt manufacturer list SV 3.2 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number, archived https://web.archive.org/web/20261102120229/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vehicle_identification_number). A WMI names the maker and plant, not the model, so a match only says the car is of a make this profile covers.
